perItemFindings.label: lem:uniform-parametric-floor
perItemFindings.one_line: `Causalean.Stat.bretagnolle_huber_affinity` requires `obsLaw M0.raw ≪ obsLaw M1.raw` and finite KL; Fintype gives measurability/integrability, but does not give absolute continuity—an in-class POMDP may assign zero mass to observed paths.

review.verbatim_critique: Re-plan `Helpers/TwoPoint.two_point_floor_explicit`: require/prove `hac` and `hfin` explicitly. For each concrete hard pair, discharge them from a proved full-support/strict-positive observed-path-mass lemma; do not claim they follow merely from finite observed-path type.

perItemFindings.label: S2 / def:minimax-risk
perItemFindings.one_line: `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` defines an unbounded estimator's `worstCaseRisk` as `0`; thus the claimed `minimaxRisk_eq_rawMinimaxRisk` using it on unrestricted `RawEstimator` is false, since unbounded raw estimators make that raw minimax value spuriously zero.

review.verbatim_critique: Keep `minimaxValue` for the bounded `ObservableEstimator` carrier, where its real-supremum conventions are sound. Drop the asserted equality to `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue rawObservedRisk`; instead record clipping as a pointwise domination establishing fidelity to the intended all-measurable infimum, or define any raw comparison with a semantics that excludes the API's unbounded-range junk convention.

perItemFindings.label: S2
perItemFindings.one_line: `minimaxValue` is type-fit, but `ObservableEstimator` receives an `ObsPath` carrying reward symbols plus `rew`; without an injectivity requirement on `rew`, this reveals distinctions between equal-valued rewards that core `O_T=(X,A,Y)` does not reveal.

review.verbatim_critique: Re-plan S1/S2 so the encoded observation is information-equivalent to `(X,A,Y)`: require `RewardMap` to be injective (with the model class restricted to its finite reward support), or quotient/map `ObsPath` to decoded reward values before passing it to estimators. Then the bounded-carrier instantiation of `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` is sound for the core observable-data experiment.

reason: Case 4a (plan/.md drift from a correct .tex) + regression pattern (c) severity-descending — rounds 5 and 6 each retired their flag and the surviving round-7 flag is narrow: the .tex fixes \(\mathsf O_T:=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^T\) with \(Y_t\in[-1,1]\) (glossary entry for \(\mathsf O_T\), and def:minimax-risk's inf over \(\sigma(\mathsf O_T,b,e,t_0,\zeta,C)\)), but S-1's Lean carrier stores the reward SYMBOL (`ObsStep nX nR := Fin nX × Bool × Fin nR`) and S-2 hands the estimator both the symbol path and `rew : RewardMap nR`, so a non-injective `rew` lets an in-carrier estimator separate equal-valued rewards — strictly more information than the .tex's observable experiment, which inflates every converse's estimator class beyond the contract. The .tex is correct and no new hypothesis is required, so stage_0 is unnecessary and stage_2/stage_3_local are unreachable/insufficient at this boundary; the per-boundary heuristic (reuse-fit ⇒ re-plan the flagged nodes) is followed.
proposed_action: Re-plan S-1 and S-2 (and propagate to def:minimax-risk plus the five converse consumers that instantiate `Causalean.Stat.le_minimaxValue_of_two_point`) so the encoded observation is information-equivalent to \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)\), WITHOUT adding any premise absent from the .tex: keep `ObsPath T nX nR` (Fintype, so the 'all measurable estimators' clause still costs nothing) and keep `rew` supplied by the model index, but add a reward-VALUE-invariance conjunct to the existing bounded subtype carrier — `ObservableEstimator T := { est : RawEstimator T // (∀ …, est … ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) ∧ (∀ nX nR b e (rew : RewardMap nR) (p p' : ObsPath T nX nR), (∀ t, ((p t).1, (p t).2.1) = ((p' t).1, (p' t).2.1) ∧ rew (p t).2.2 = rew (p' t).2.2) → est nX nR b e rew p = est nX nR b e rew p') }` — i.e. every estimator factors through the decoded path \(t\mapsto(X_t,A_t,\mathrm{rew}(R_t))\). Record in S-2 that (i) this only NARROWS the carrier, so the inf-sup is if anything larger and every converse stays valid, (ii) the note's own \(\widehat\theta_k\) (scores \(Z_t(k)=Y_t\prod\rho_j\)) touches the reward only through `rew`, hence is invariant by construction and the achievability side still attains inside the carrier, and (iii) the two hard families' shared `rew = ![-1,1]` is injective, so the TWO-POINT DISCIPLINE clause of S-2 is unaffected. Explicitly REJECT the alternative fix of requiring `RewardMap` injective with the model class restricted to its finite reward support: that would strengthen \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) beyond ass:pomdp-kernel / ass:bounded-reward and is a forbidden silent assumption. Change nothing else — the round-5 full-support discharge of `hac`/`hfin` (P10, `signedDepth_fullSupportObs`) and the round-6 junk-free domination ledger (P11, dropping `minimaxRisk_eq_rawMinimaxRisk`) are accepted and must be preserved verbatim.

perItemFindings.label: S2
perItemFindings.one_line: `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` is sound generically, but its planned `ObservableEstimator` receives the whole coding map `rew`; the within-fixed-`rew` RewardValueInvariant condition does not prevent dependence on `rew` itself, including unobserved symbols/codings. The core permits only functions of `(X_t,A_t,Y_t)`, b, e, regime parameters, and observed-state alphabet.

review.verbatim_critique: Re-plan S2/def:minimax-risk so the estimator carrier is natural across reward encodings (or directly takes decoded real-reward paths with the required measurability condition). Do not expose `rew` as a model-specific side input merely to decode a finite-symbol PMF; fixed-`rew` fiber invariance alone leaves an information leak and makes the minimax reuse instantiate the wrong observable experiment.

perItemFindings.label: S1
perItemFindings.one_line: P1 encodes rewards as a finite alphabet `Fin nR`, but the core permits arbitrary bounded real rewards via `K(dy,...)`; this silently shrinks the model class, so the planned upper bounds prove only a finite-support subclass.

review.verbatim_critique: Replan S1/S2 to preserve the core's real-valued bounded reward law, or establish a genuine equivalence. The recorded finite-support restriction is not faithful for the core headline; matching lower and upper bounds only within the restricted subclass does not repair it.

perItemFindings.label: S1
perItemFindings.one_line: `FullView T := Fin T -> FullStep` contains only S₁,…,S_T, but `PomdpKernelLaw` is proposed for every `t : Fin T` with next block `(Y_t,X_{t+1},H_{t+1})`; the terminal transition/state S_{T+1} is absent, so the local compProd world cannot realize the core sampling model.

review.verbatim_critique: Re-plan S1's local trajectory carrier and its history projections: carry T actions/rewards together with T+1 joint states (or an equivalent endpoint-inclusive representation), then state the compProd factorization against that carrier. This is an encoding/world defect, not a defect in the core mathematics.

reason: Case 4a (Lean/plan drift rooted in the .md world layer) + regression pattern (b): three consecutive rounds each flagged a DIFFERENT facet of the same defect — the .md's local world carriers do not realize the .tex sampling model (S2 estimator carrier leaking the coding map `rew`; S1 `Fin nR` finite reward alphabet against the .tex's real bounded reward kernel `K(dy,dx',dh'|x,h,a)` with `Y_t ∈ [-1,1]` per ass:bounded-reward; S1 `FullView T := Fin T → FullStep` omitting the terminal state S_{T+1} demanded by the per-`t` `PomdpKernelLaw` factorization).
